profile.headline: Radar Software Engineer at Waymo
profile.summary:
Electrical Engineer in the Electromagnetics Research Group (EMRG) working on millimeter-wave sensors for intelligent mobility. 

Significant experience writing C++ software for autonomous driving including low-level CAN drivers for vehicle actuation, waypoint following via RTK GNSS with pure pursuit path planner, high-definition (HD) map parsing, graph calculation, graph traversal, and visualization, and sensor hardware drivers for networked radar in robot operating system (ROS).

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: As a graduate research assistant in the EMRG group at MSU I've had the opportunity to learn and develop design methods for microwave and millimeter-wave radar subsystems.  I am also a member of the SAE Autodrive Challenge team where we are actively developing an autonomous vehicle.

positions.title: Autodrive Challenge (SAE) - HD Mapping Lead, Localization and Controls Engineer
positions.description:
• Created ROS package which converts coarse UTM waypoints to lane lines using protobuf HD map and Boost Graph Library (BGL) for Dykstra shortest-route at MCity
• Implemented (with others) waypoint following demo using Chevy Bolt, Novatel PwrPak7-E1 GNSS/INS with RTK corrections for localization, tuned controller values based on RMS path error
• Improved ROS/ CAN vehicle interface by opening Linux socketCAN sockets directly in ROS nodes instead of using third-party ROS conversion node
• Developed ROS driver for Continental ARS430 FMCW automotive radar with visualization node for radar detections including display of normalized RCS
• Modified Autoware pure pursuit waypoint following algorithm to increase path availability and robustness (removed failure modes associated with current position greater than consecutive waypoint distance and current perpendicular foot greater than search radius)

positions.title: Teaching Assistant- ECE 491: Creating Autonomous Vehicles
positions.description:
• Created ROS labs (with others) covering robotics basics such as reading sensor data, actuating the robot, and simulation and visualization
• Created material covering ROS install, TurtleBot3 packages install from GIT, Turtlebot3 bringup and simulation in Gazebo, subscribing to and viewing topic data in RVIZ , and robot state publisher basics such as rqt_tf_tree
• Created ROS material covering the Autorace package including robot actuation, twist conversion, and obstacle detection and avoidance
• Helped students develop code and debug programs running on TurtleBot3 hardware
• Guided individual group vision based line-following project using classical CV methods

positions.title: Lab Instructor- MIT Deeptech Bootcamp
positions.description:
• Developed TurtleBot3 lab and line-following competition
• Helped assemble, install Ubuntu MATE, ROS, and lab code on 10 robots for bootcamp teams
• Taught students SSH with X-forwarding and using TMUX for ROS sessions
• Instructed students on using and modifying launch files, sending velocity commands, and camera interface bring-up
• Gave hints for adjusting PID parameters to tune robot for vision-based line-following
• Updated code base on the fly to deal with unexpected hardware upgrade from Raspberry Pi 3 Model B to Model B+

positions.title: Electrical Engineer
positions.description: At Tecniq I was responsible for developing firmware, PC GUI's, and cross-platform mobile applications for wireless control of lighting systems.  In addition, I designed schematics and PCB's for LED drivers and controllers while performing thermal and EMC analysis.

publications.title: Automotive Velocity Sensing Using Millimeter-Wave Interferometric Radar
Radar Tracking With Orthogonal Velocity Measurements for Autonomous Ground Vehicles
